drug_class: PCSK9 inhibitor (a type of cholesterol-lowering injectable medication)
purpose: Alirocumab is used to lower bad cholesterol (LDL) in your blood. It is used in adults who have heart disease or a genetic condition that causes very high cholesterol, especially when diet changes and other cholesterol medicines like statins are not enough on their own.
how_it_works: Your liver makes a protein called PCSK9 that breaks down the receptors your body uses to remove bad cholesterol from your blood. Alirocumab blocks that protein, so more receptors stay active and your liver can remove more LDL cholesterol from your bloodstream. Think of it as unclogging the drain so your body can flush out more bad cholesterol.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include redness, soreness, bruising, or itching at the injection site. Some people also experience a runny nose, sore throat, flu-like symptoms, or mild back and joint pain.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using this medication. Let your doctor know about all other medications you take. Rarely, some people may have a serious allergic reaction including rash, hives, or swelling of the face and throat — seek emergency help right away if this happens. This medication is not recommended for children.
typical_dosing: Alirocumab is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous) every 2 weeks or once a month, depending on your dose. The usual starting dose is 75 mg every 2 weeks, and your doctor may increase it to 150 mg every 2 weeks if needed. It comes in a prefilled pen or syringe that you can use at home after training from your healthcare provider.
